rows.title: gcode
rows.summary: Create machining toolpaths for the staged workpiece in PowerMill and deliver the required NC output.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing) engineer using Autodesk PowerMill.

## Your Task
Design toolpaths to machine workpiece **125162_319** using the provided blank PowerMill project.

## Input Files
- **PowerMill project** (blank, with pre-configured tools, zero toolpaths):
  `125162_319\input\125162-319-NCFM-T`
- **Ideal workpiece geometry** (.prt format): `125162_319\input\125162_319.prt`
- **Reference image**: `125162_319\input\125162_319.jpg`

## What You Must Do
1. Copy the PowerMill project from `125162_319\input\125162-319-NCFM-T` to `125162_319\output\125162-319-NCFM-T`
   (work on the copy so the original stays intact)
2. Open PowerMill from `125162_319\software\PowerMill 2025.lnk` and load the copied project at:
   `125162_319\output\125162-319-NCFM-T`
3. Study the ideal workpiece geometry (.prt file) to understand the target shape.
   The copied PowerMill project already contains the machine, stock, tool library,
   and workpiece setup; the `.prt` file is an external geometry reference.
4. Design toolpaths that will machine the workpiece from raw stock:
   - Use roughing toolpaths to remove bulk material
   - Use finishing toolpaths for surfaces requiring higher precision
   - Use the pre-configured tools already in the project (do NOT create new tools)
5. **Critical**: Ensure each toolpath has NO collisions and NO gouging
6. Run a stock model simulation to confirm the final result
7. **Save** the PowerMill project (Ctrl+S)

## Color Coding on the Workpiece
The .prt file has faces colored by precision requirement:
- Tight tolerance faces (e.g., VDI12/15): require finer finish toolpaths
- Loose tolerance faces (e.g., spray/texture faces): standard finish is acceptable

## Quality Requirements
- The stock simulation must complete without collisions or gouging
- The machined geometry must reproduce the supplied `.prt` target accurately
- Keep critical finished surfaces within 0.3 mm and all modeled surfaces within 2.0 mm

## Important
- Work ONLY within the project at `125162_319\output\125162-319-NCFM-T`
- Do NOT move or rename the project folder
- SAVE your project when finished
agent_must_do: Open the staged blank PowerMill project for the selected workpiece.
Review the staged `.prt` geometry and `.jpg` visual reference.
Design roughing and finishing toolpaths using the preconfigured tool library.
Ensure the toolpaths have no collisions and no gouges.
Run a stock-model simulation in PowerMill.

rows.title: mold-flow
rows.summary: Configure process parameters in Moldex3D, run the staged mold-flow analysis, and save the required outputs.
rows.task_prompt:
You are a CAE (Computer-Aided Engineering) engineer performing injection molding simulation using Moldex3D.

## Your Task
Configure process parameters and run a mold-flow analysis for project **230057** using the Moldex3D software.

## Input Files
- **Moldex3D project** (mesh + material already configured, NO process parameters or analysis results):
  `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\4穴230057`
- **Process specification**: `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\process_spec.json`
  This JSON file contains all the injection molding parameters you must configure.
- **Results template**: `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\results_template.json`
  This JSON file has fields with null values that you must reproduce in `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\output\results.json`.
- **Part geometry** (.x_t Parasolid): `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\230057.x_t` (for visual reference only)

## What You Must Do
1. Open Moldex3D from `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\software\MDXStudio.lnk` and load the project at:
   `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\4穴230057`
2. Read the process specification JSON carefully
3. Configure ALL process parameters in Moldex3D's Process Wizard:
   - Melt temperature, mold temperature
   - Injection flow rate profile
   - V/P switch point (volume filled %)
   - Packing pressure profile and time
   - Cooling time, coolant temperature, coolant flow rate
4. Set up the analysis sequence: **Fill → Pack → Cool (Transient) → Warp**
4. Use the optional `.x_t` CAD file as a visual cross-check if helpful
5. Run the full analysis (this may take 1-2 hours)
6. After analysis completes, extract the simulation results from the Moldex3D result viewer
7. Create `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\output\results.json` using the same JSON structure as `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\results_template.json` and fill in all null fields with the simulation values
8. Save any working project artifacts under `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\output` if you choose to create a writable copy

## Results to Extract
After analysis completes, fill in these fields in results.json:
- **Max injection pressure** (MPa)
- **V/P switch pressure** (MPa)
- **Runner pressure drop** (MPa)
- **Max clamping force** (ton)
- **Filling time** (sec)
- **Estimated cooling time** (sec)
- **Cycle time** (sec)
- **Part weight** per cavity (g)
- **Part volume** per cavity (cc)

## Evaluation
Your work will be evaluated by comparing your results.json against the reference values.
Each field within ±1% tolerance of the reference scores 1 point.
Final score = fraction of correct fields.

## Important
- Treat `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\4穴230057` as the staged clean baseline
- Do not modify or rename the staged input project in place
- SAVE your project when finished
- The results template at `E:\agenthle\engineering\mold-flow\230057\input\results_template.json` shows the exact JSON structure expected

Run the Fill → Pack → Cool (Transient) → Warp analysis sequence.
Extract the required simulation values after the run completes.
Fill `output/results.json` using the staged template structure.

rows.title: Sanding Performance Image Scoring
rows.summary: Compute pixel-level paint-removal scores from reference and sanded panel images, then write a structured CSV with quantity, uniformity, and composite metrics.
rows.task_prompt:
You are completing a sanding-performance image scoring task on a Windows VM.

Input files are staged in:
`base\input`

Read `algorithm_spec.md` in that directory. It defines how to use the reference images `panel_painted.png` and `panel_unpainted.png` to score:
- `panel_sanded_01.png`
- `panel_sanded_02.png`
- `panel_sanded_03.png`

Use RGB image values and follow the formulas in `algorithm_spec.md`.

Write exactly one output file:
`base\output\sanding_scores.csv`

The CSV must have this header:
`panel_id,quantity_pct,uniformity_pct,composite_pct`

It must contain exactly one row for each sanded panel:
- `panel_sanded_01`
- `panel_sanded_02`
- `panel_sanded_03`

Round the three numeric metric columns to one decimal place. Do not modify the files under `input/`.
agent_must_do: Read the visible algorithm specification and five panel images from the staged input directory.
Compute quantity, uniformity, and composite sanding scores for each of the three sanded panels.
Write `sanding_scores.csv` under the runtime output directory with the required schema and one row per sanded panel.

input_files.name: algorithm_spec.md
input_files.description: Visible task algorithm and output schema.
